_comment: Machine-readable learning-behavior contract. Each invariant has an ID, a severity, and the test-name substrings that must have at least one passing test. learn-check fails if an active invariant has no passing test, or if a listed test name matches nothing. Changing behavior means editing this file AND its tests AND the implementation together (the 'revise door' — see CONTRACT.md).

invariants.statement: A grade turn must not render unless an agreeing grade-audit receipt is present; a missing receipt is withheld with NO_GRADE_AUDIT_PASS. One batched `items[]` envelope may carry several learner answers, and a mismatch surfaces the per-item corrections. Only the newest grade verdict may block: a stale `agrees:false` receipt is superseded by a corrected agreeing re-dispatch, so it cannot poison every later grade turn.

invariants.statement: The gate checks omission, not just commission. In a teach/resume flow a `claims` turn must declare a valid `turn_kind`: `plan`, `triage`, `attack`, `hint`, `autopsy`, `answer`, `repair`, `grade_feedback`, or `idea`. A `triage` turn ships a non-empty `triage[]` where every row names an item and a valid bucket and every non-solid row carries the learner's quote or a source citation; optional `requires`/`on_path` fields order the attack plan and must be acyclic. An `attack` turn ships exactly one subtype from the menu (`mechanism`/`counterexample`/`perturbation`/`source_clash`/`sabotage`/`synthesis`). An `autopsy` turn ships exactly one reasoning `step` — `index`/`total`/`fact`/`rests_on`/`check` — with the `fact` and `check` prose present in the draft; more than one step is a lecture, so it is withheld. `plan`/`answer`/`repair`/`hint`/`grade_feedback` need no shape block. An `idea` turn (a new definition, formula, mechanism, or micro-step the learner actually asked for) carries all four beats — `problem`, `where_from`, `conditions`, `contrast` — each non-empty and its prose present in the verified draft; `where_from` asks for conceptual entailment, not a symbolic derivation. A missing or unknown `turn_kind`, a malformed `triage[]`, an attack without one valid subtype, or an autopsy without one bound step is withheld (`FOUNDATION_INCOMPLETE`) with a remedy naming the fix, so a fluent what-only lecture, an ungrounded triage claim, a chain of attacks, or a multi-step patch cannot render as if complete. Foundation beats are also the completeness rubric for the learner's own model: a missing beat is an attack target, never a Tutor paragraph. A fact-check verdict naming a non-empty `omitted_foundations[]` is an `ISSUES` verdict even when it also says PASS; the omission check is scoped to load-bearing conceptual gaps and never demands a missing symbolic derivation.

invariants.statement: At the retry cap, a claims turn whose draft states hard facts (extractHardFacts: URL, LaTeX/math expression, scientific notation, decimal, percentage, or 3+ digit integer) is withheld entirely — only the banner renders, no content — rather than delivered as `⛔ UNVERIFIED`, but only when the block implicates verification (`FACT_CHECK_*`, `CLAIMS_INCOMPLETE`, `FOUNDATION_INCOMPLETE`, `NO_FACT_CHECK_MATCH`). A foundation-incomplete idea turn (`FOUNDATION_INCOMPLETE`) is withheld the same way even with no hard facts, so a complete-sounding but foundation-less summary is never shown. A verified draft blocked only on context (`NO_SCOUT_CONTEXT`/`NO_REVIEW_CONTEXT`) degrades gracefully. Non-hard-fact prose still degrades with the UNVERIFIED banner, and G-retry-cap semantics are unchanged for every other turn (grade/quiz/none). This deliberately inverts the anti-dead-end policy for load-bearing facts and for the missing theoretical foundation.

invariants.statement: The content gate (fact-check/quiz/grade/review) and the state gate are split. The block is subject to the standard retry cap: a persistent, unfixable error withholds twice and then degrades to `⛔ UNVERIFIED` rather than dead-ending the close.

invariants.statement: One pi RPC session per chat, reused across turns; only the newest user message of each posted transcript is forwarded (pi owns its context). The session is started with a deterministic `--session-id`, so a bridge restart or a pi crash resumes the same transcript instead of starting blank and re-deriving context from the state repo. A resend of the same message is a regenerate: the bridge forks the session back to that user message before re-prompting, and falls back to appending if the fork fails.

invariants.statement: Deleting an Open WebUI chat removes its pi session: the background sweep first proves the API key with the chat-list probe, then asks Open WebUI about every `chat-<id>` session and closes/removes it on a per-chat 401/404/422 (Open WebUI reports a missing chat as 401). A network error, an invalid key, a server error, an existing chat, or a turn still in flight never deletes a transcript; an in-flight session is retried on the next sweep.

invariants.statement: Each posted Open WebUI transcript is aligned with the previous turn's visible user-message list before prompting (falling back to pi's own user messages after a restart). A new message appends; a regenerate re-answers the last user; an edited/replaced/truncated user message forks pi at the replaced turn first; and a Continue click (the transcript ends with the assistant being extended) sends a marked continuation prompt without forking. Continue markers are excluded from alignment so a later turn is not misread as an edit; a compacted transcript (Open WebUI's `[CONVERSATION SUMMARY]` system message) appends/continues without dropping pi's older context; and when pi's user list cannot be read the bridge falls back to the old last-message heuristic.

invariants.statement: When a streaming client disconnects, the bridge treats it as Open WebUI Stop: it sends pi `abort`, drains the turn to settlement, and returns so a canceled turn neither keeps working nor holds the single-writer learning lock. A socket watcher notices EOF even while pi is silent inside a long tool call. `--no-abort-on-disconnect` (or `PI_BRIDGE_ABORT_ON_DISCONNECT=false`) restores the old consume-to-settlement behavior.

invariants.statement: The Tutor is a sparring partner and stress-tester, not a primary teacher. The pi/Open WebUI layer ships the same interrogation stance as the Antigravity layer: never teach a topic cold, read the learner's material, require a closed-book model, bracket the edge when the model is ambiguous, triage the model as a dependency-ordered attack tree, attack one hole at a time, reveal at most one reasoning step when a legal reveal is delivered, patch the learner's model (v1 -> breaking case -> v2), run the entailment check, and graduate it with a naive-student clone. The retired teacher-first loop (probe -> plan -> mini-checkpoint lecture) is gone from the prompt resources; the bracket is diagnostic measurement, not a lecture.

invariants.statement: A teach/resume `turn_kind:"triage"` turn carries a non-empty `triage[]`; every row has an item and a bucket in solid|missing|suspect, and every non-solid row carries grounding (the learner's exact words for suspect, a source citation for missing). Optional `requires` names the rows whose repair must land first and `on_path` marks the shortest dependency path to the model's goal; a reference to an unknown row, a self-reference, a duplicate item name, or a cycle is withheld (`FOUNDATION_INCOMPLETE`) with a triage-specific remedy, so the attack plan is always traversable. A missing/empty table, an invalid bucket, or an ungrounded non-solid row withholds the turn the same way.

invariants.statement: A teach/resume `turn_kind:"attack"` turn declares exactly one subtype from the attack menu. A missing, unknown, or multiple subtype withholds the turn (FOUNDATION_INCOMPLETE) with an attack-specific remedy. The verifier additionally rejects an attack that does not target a non-solid triage row, an attack on a dependent hole before its `requires` are solid, a counterexample that does not satisfy the learner's statement as written, a perturbation of a cosmetic term, or an attack that fills the hole (SPOONFEEDING_DETECTED / LECTURE_SLIP).

invariants.statement: Every teach/resume claims turn declares a valid turn_kind. `plan`, `triage`, `attack`, `hint`, `autopsy`, `answer`, `repair`, and `grade_feedback` need no foundation beat; only `idea` does. A grade-feedback turn is a claims turn verified with `turn_kind:"grade_feedback"` + `grade_verdicts[]`; it must reproduce the audited verdicts exactly and never expose verification internals.

invariants.statement: Teaching mode is a repair, not a lesson. After a graded miss the learner first gets the hint ladder (R0-R2 + a source return) and one self-repair attempt; structural misses get one verification nudge first, and a `missing` gap has nothing to cue and enters repair mode at once. Re-attacking the same gap, or re-asking the same item, without a repair turn once that attempt has failed is REPAIR_MODE_SKIPPED. The trigger is verifier-enforced (fact-check 4c); the gate enforces the receipt that follows.

invariants.statement: A `turn_kind:"repair"` turn ships a `repair` block bound to exactly one `gap`, naming the diagnosed `miss_class` (cue|discrimination|execution|structural - a careless miss is re-checked, never repaired, and a `missing` triage row uses the class grade-audit returned, usually cue) and the `tactic` that diagnosis selects (source_return|retrieval_cue|contrasting_pair|worked_step|push_down|full_teach), with `status:"teaching"|"done"`. A `teaching` turn ships exactly one reasoning `step` (index/total/fact/rests_on/check) whose `fact` and `check` prose are in the draft - a multi-step repair is a lecture and is withheld. The verifier enforces the method: start from the unconditional truth the gap rests on, one motivated step at a time, Socratic first (expository only when beyond cold reach or the learner asked to be told), check every step, never build on an undemonstrated step, no wall of text (LECTURE_SLIP).

invariants.statement: A repair turn teaches only its bound gap, never the wider curriculum, and the learner still authors the model: the Tutor never writes, polishes, or merges v1/v2 (MODEL_GHOSTWRITING). Widening a repair into a lesson is REPAIR_SCOPE_DRIFT.

invariants.statement: An open repair blocks the attack battery: a `turn_kind:"attack"` turn is withheld (NO_REPAIR_RECEIPT) while any repair is open - including at the retry cap, so a soft attack can never leak the battery - and a second gap cannot be opened before the first is closed (REPAIR_INCOMPLETE). A repair is closed only by a `status:"done"` turn naming (a) the fresh-surface check the learner already answered and grade-audit passed, bound to the graded item with `repair_gap` equal to this repair's gap (never to prose or to a check graded for another gap), and (b) the learner's own-words restatement, quoted verbatim. A done turn with no graded pass, a mismatched gap, or no restatement is withheld (REPAIR_INCOMPLETE). The fresh-surface check must not re-ask the repair turn's own question or be answerable by reciting its prose (quiz-audit repair rule); a recital is SHALLOW_PASS (grade-audit).

invariants.statement: The fixed verifier prompts police mental-model integrity as strictly as truth. `fact-check` audits attack grounding, dependency ordering, and counterexample validity, triage integrity, model ghostwriting, ungrounded holes, lecture slips, one-step autopsy patches, spoonfeeding, cue leakage, and visual sufficiency (visual_plan present; VISUAL_PLAN_MISSING / VISUAL_MISSED). `grade-audit` grades the mechanism and the direction/extreme check, applies the attack and battery rubrics, flags SHALLOW_PASS when the learner merely remixes the Tutor's recent turns, records sure-but-fail as false confidence, grades the graduation conceptual entailment without demanding algebra, and requires a real `naive_student_receipt` for a clone. `quiz-audit` enforces context-appropriate item types (bracket probe, pre-attack prediction, practice, review, solo), the concept-label ban, the qualitative-trace requirement, and check craft.

invariants.statement: Graduation for a concept/design runs an entailment check before the naive-student clone: one qualitative question asking why the patched claim must hold given what the learner already accepted, and what would have to be true for it to break. Pass requires the learner's own conceptual one-step entailment plus the breaking condition; this is not a symbolic derivation and must not demand algebra. The clone then hands over v2 verbatim (never a Tutor paraphrase) plus the concept, a seeded misconception, prerequisite level, and a qualitative prediction/tool-choice task. The clone reports NAIVE_STUDENT_RECEIPT with task_succeeded and questions_unanswered; a failed clone is a fail regardless of the claimed verdict, a missing receipt is an ISSUES verdict, and the outcome is logged as feynman_pass/feynman_fail. v1 and v2 are preserved verbatim in order with the breaking case labelled between them.
tests: naive-student runs the clone protocol

invariants.statement: Review and solo batches test cue selection and transfer, not recognition: no MCQs (MCQs are legal only in a bracket probe), items are unlabeled for selection/application, and the learner must produce the 3-line qualitative trace (cue & principle -> mechanism/knob-turn -> direction & extreme check). Review/solo batches include operational items (perturbation, misapplication, decoy/near-miss). A review presents verified feedback and pauses for learner questions before any state is persisted; `review-clerk` runs only on an explicit "no questions".

invariants.statement: The knowledge graph is world knowledge, never learner state. `Knowledge Wiki/graph/nodes.jsonl` records subject-matter propositions (short name, one self-contained statement, verbatim aliases, provenance); `chains.jsonl` records reasoning chains (a premise set that jointly entails a conclusion, with provenance). No mastery, verdict, confidence, attempt, grade, score, level, or "the learner understands X" ever enters the ledgers — a misconception enters as its true correction. The merge CLI rejects any record field outside the ledger schema, and the graph-audit flags LEARNER_STATE_LEAK.
tests: test_learner_state_field_is_rejected

invariants.statement: The graph is provenance-anchored and append-only: every proposition and chain carries at least one provenance point naming the source file it came from, and a re-encounter appends a link line whose verbatim phrasing joins `aliases[]` and whose provenance unions with the define line — never overwriting the original statement. The ledgers are written only through `pi/graph.py merge`/`retract` (Clerk-run during ingest); no agent hand-edits the JSONL.

invariants.statement: Edges are not stored. The rendered graph is a derived, lossy view in which each reasoning chain becomes an implication node (premises -> implication -> conclusion), so two independent arguments for one conclusion stay two diamonds instead of a manufactured fan-in. Re-asserting an identical premise set/conclusion links the existing chain instead of duplicating it, and retracting a proposition drops every chain that depends on it (reported as dropped, never silently kept).

invariants.statement: Graph extraction is an ingest duty: the Clerk distils the session's taught propositions and reasoning chains with `graph-extract`, merges them deterministically, and the parent dispatches an independent `graph-audit` over every written id (created and linked propositions/chains) before the ingest closes. The close is gate-enforced: the summary is withheld (NO_GRAPH_AUDIT_PASS) until a passing audit covers every id in CLERK_WRITES.graph, and an ISSUES verdict (any severity) withholds it (GRAPH_AUDIT_ISSUES) until the Clerk records a fix (retract/correct and re-merge) and a fresh audit returns zero issues — no cycle cap — and the ledgers are never hand-edited to satisfy the audit. The audit fact-checks the connections too: every chain premise and conclusion is grounded in the cited material and jointly entails it, and every link joins the same proposition.

invariants.statement: Cross-session attacks cite the learner's actual prior words: the fact-check envelope carries `prior_knowledge` (prior verbatim models, graph propositions/chains, open mistakes) and every quoted prior item appears verbatim in it. The clash must target the same concept/mental model under interrogation, both sides are verbatim, and no winner is announced — attacks keep their existing subtypes and the one-attack-per-turn rule. An invented, paraphrased, or drift-merged "you once said…" is PRIOR_UNGROUNDED; a prior fact about a different concept is not a valid attack target.

invariants.statement: Lesson and review digests carry `prior_knowledge` harvested from the durable provenance graph (`pi/graph.py list`) plus prior verbatim learner models and open mistakes, so cross-session grounding never depends on the Tutor's memory. The digest's arrays may be empty when nothing relevant exists, but a failed graph read must appear as a visible `failed_refs` entry rather than a silent empty. The digest quote is data, never a learner-facing summary.

invariants.statement: Hints follow the R0–R5 ladder (attention redirect → pattern re-description → candidate class → proposition named → move outlined → worked step), one rung per request, chosen to answer the first break in the learner's trace — the stall is not always where their attention is. Statement repairs are free and immediate; solution information is metered (one rung). The rung needed is a difficulty readout (R3 or above means the item was over the edge). The independence budget still caps rungs (2/1/0), and solo sessions get no hints at all.

The classification layers on the unchanged `error_type` enum (structural|deviation|application|metacognitive); no new error_type values are introduced, and a class the verifier did not supply is never invented.

invariants.statement: Review and practice items are retrieval from an inactive state: targets are interleaved, a concept is not re-asked immediately after its verdict, and items are built around decision points where a not-yet-active proposition must be selected. Difficulty targets retrieval that succeeds with effort (~85% per retrieval event), and a hint rescues the learner at the edge instead of lowering the demand. The 3-line qualitative trace is the minimum working trace, not a cap on how much thinking the learner may submit.

invariants.statement: Quiz questions and grade items may carry `targets[]`, the knowledge-graph record ids (`n_…` propositions / `arg_…` chains) the item retrieves. Targets are additive record-keeping, never learner-facing text and never a grading input: the binding fields are unchanged, a missing or empty target list blocks nothing, and `grade-audit` ignores targets when deciding a verdict. Ids are copied verbatim from the scout digest's `prior_knowledge` (never invented), carried from question to grade item to `REVIEW_WRITES.grade_verdicts[]`, and recorded on the attempt by `ops.py attempt --targets`; malformed ids are `TARGETS_INVALID` at quiz-audit, and `ops.py attempt|amend` rejects both malformed and non-live ids (missing or retracted), so only current graph records are recorded. A digest snapshot that names a stale id is dropped rather than resolved or replaced. They are the bridge to per-node mastery and never enter the graph ledger as learner state. Per-node mastery aggregation is not implemented — the targets are the plumbing — and `ops.py mastery` remains per-concept.
